Bard level 1 adds no new hit die; later bard dice add to retained earlier hit points.
Use the bard spell table, retained fighter/thief abilities, and most favorable applicable saving throws.

progression.label: Special sequential progression
progression.description: Fighter → thief → bard under Appendix II’s own rules. The supplemental class requires DM acceptance and a human or half-elf with Strength, Wisdom, Dexterity, and Charisma 15+, Intelligence 12+, and Constitution 10+. Change from fighter after reaching level 5 and before level 8; the thief-stage transition is worded “between 5th and 9th.” Bard XP is counted separately, with earlier abilities retained as specified.

classes.name: Cavalier
classes.description: A chivalric mounted-warrior class with social qualifications, possible zero-level stages, and its own conduct code. The original table's hit-die heading conflicts with other text; errata must be identified separately.
guidance: Requires Strength, Dexterity, Constitution 15 and Intelligence, Wisdom 10; confirm service, social station, sponsorship, and any zero-level stages.
At each higher level, increase the Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution percentiles by the specified 2d10 procedure.
Below the self-training threshold, train with a cavalier of at least level 4 or two levels higher, whichever is greater.
After reaching level 6, the normal regimen suffices for training; mount and weapon abilities continue to change.

UA p. 13 Table II lists the cavalier for any armor, shield, and weapons, subject to note 1’s social-station limits on armor and arms; note 2 bars oil in personal combat but permits siege use, and poison is listed only if evil. Use the six social-station packages on p. 25; each horse is supplied with station-appropriate tack, harness, saddle, and saddlebags, and a cavalier below Upper Class begins as a 0-level Horseman to be taken in by a good family and esquired.

UA p. 26 lists the cavalier weapon-proficiency row as 3*, a −3 nonproficiency penalty, and one added proficiency per two levels. Its star note specifies 0-level Horseman/Lancer and 1st-level Armiger counts and restricts Cavalier weapon choices.
errata: Project-supplied correction: cavalier hit dice are d10. This correction is kept separate from the original printing’s conflicting hit-die heading. An authoritative errata document has not yet been checked in this release.

classes.name: Barbarian
classes.description: A hardy fighter subclass with wilderness talents, changing magic restrictions, and a separate XP progression. The UA XP table is transcribed.
guidance: Human and non-lawful: Strength 15, Dexterity 14, Constitution 15; Wisdom may not exceed 16.
No prime requisite grants bonus XP, and a player barbarian cannot be a two-class character.
Update class skills and the level-based ability to harm creatures otherwise requiring magical weapons.
After level 8, gain 4 hp per level instead of another hit die; check changing restrictions on magic use.
UA p. 13 Table II permits any armor, shield, and weapons, but note 3 limits the class Dexterity armor benefit in bulky or fairly bulky armor.

UA p. 18 requires the barbarian’s initial weapon proficiencies to include hand axe, knife, and spear; other weapons based on the native area may be chosen by the DM. The p. 26 weapon table lists six initial proficiencies, a −1 nonproficiency penalty, and one added proficiency per two levels; these weapon slots are separate from the barbarian’s nonweapon abilities.

UA pp. 19–20 group barbarian abilities as eight primary abilities (climbing, hiding, surprise, back protection, leaping/springing, detecting illusion, detecting magic, leadership), four secondary abilities (survival, first aid, outdoor craft, tracking), and one or more locale- or culture-selected tertiary skills. All four secondary abilities are possessed, but are generally limited in unfamiliar areas until about a month of continuous exposure; the DM determines applicable tertiary skills. Paddled and rowed small craft are separate tertiary options.

UA p. 20 names eight locale- or culture-selected tertiary skill options: animal handling, horsemanship, long-distance signalling, running, small craft (paddled), small craft (rowed), sound imitation, and snare building. The DM determines which apply to the campaign; a barbarian has one or more.

classes.name: Thief-acrobat
classes.description: A specialist path entered after ordinary thief levels. Its specialist XP thresholds and conversion procedure are supplied.
guidance: Requires Strength 15 and Dexterity 16, and five completed thief levels.
On qualifying for level 6, train for six weeks under a thief-acrobat of at least level 10.
Pick pockets, opening locks, and finding/removing traps stop improving at their level-5 ability; magical writing is never gained.

Use the specialist acrobatics tables and explicit climbing progression. UA pp.23 and 25 describe stopped, retained and generally inherited thief abilities; later progression of the four retained skills remains a campaign interpretation.

UA p. 13 Table II lists the Acrobat’s armor as “as thief,” no shield, and weapons “as thief, plus lasso and staff”; oil is permitted and poison is the DM’s option. Note 4 directs armor other than leather to the function adjustments in Thieves Table II (p. 22).

UA p. 25 Tables II and III adjust the Acrobat’s base function chances or maxima for Strength and Dexterity; apply their stated racial adjustments as well. Table IV separates body-associated weight (clothing, accessories, armor, weapons) from additional carried weight, which applies only while tightrope walking; backpacks are otherwise barred during Acrobat activities. Its level-14 extra 1,000 gp and level-22 passenger examples are limited by the accompanying procedure.
UA p. 26 lists the Acrobat weapon-proficiency row as 2 initial weapons, a −3 nonproficiency penalty, and one added proficiency per four levels.

classes.name: Paladin · UA revision
classes.description: UA makes the paladin a cavalier subclass. PHB paladin powers and level advancement remain in force, with additional cavalier features and revised entry requirements.
guidance: Meet cavalier requirements plus Wisdom 13 and Charisma 17; remain lawful good.
Correct social station or noble sponsorship is required; sponsorship can require both zero-level stages.
UA removes the prime requisite and its exceptional-ability XP bonus.
Apply cavalier weapon, parry, horsemanship, fear, saving-throw, and ability-improvement features, including Charisma improvement.

Source conflict in the ordinary thrusting/striking weapon attack table: UA p.22 puts level 12 in both 7–12 at 3 attacks/2 rounds and 12–18 at 2/round. The stated under-one-HD/normal-human melee case and fighter/ranger specialization use separate rules. PHB p.25 instead begins 2/round at 13th. classes.name: Druid · UA high levels
classes.description: UA extends the druid hierarchy through Grand Druid and a separate Hierophant progression. The XP reset makes a simple level-1 cumulative array unsuitable.
guidance: The Grand Druid is level 15, with at least 3,000,001 XP; the office carries special responsibilities and benefits.
After at least 3,500,001 XP, a Grand Druid may seek a successor and abdicate.
On entering the level-16 Hierophant path, the XP total resets to 1 and office-related bonus spells are relinquished.
Use the separate Hierophant table and planar abilities; do not extrapolate the PHB druid table.

UA p. 13 Table II restricts the Druid to leather or padded armor, a wooden shield, and the listed weapons (aklys, club, dagger, dart, garrot, hammer, lasso, sap, sling, scimitar, spear, staff, staff sling, sword (khopesh), and whip); oil is permitted and poison is the DM’s option.
UA p. 26 lists the Druid weapon-proficiency row as 2 initial weapons, a −4 nonproficiency penalty, and one added proficiency per five levels.

changes: Grand Druid eligibility begins at 3,000,001 XP; the office knows six spells of each spell level and gains the stated extra six spell levels, subject to the unique office and service conditions.

changes: After at least 3,500,001 XP as Grand Druid, find a successor and abdicate to enter the Hierophant path: reset XP to 1 and relinquish the office-related extra spell levels.
Spell-slot maxima stay at six per spell level; future advancement changes casting level and grants special powers instead of additional slots.
Gain immunity to natural animal/vegetable poisons (including monster poisons), but not mineral poisons or poison gas; gain 160 extra years of life and vigorous health.

You can alter appearance non-magically in 1 segment: height and weight up to 50% either way, apparent age from child to very old, and human/humanoid features; true seeing or similar perception can reveal it.

For elemental conjuring, UA replaces the earth results and supplies further tables. A roll equal to or below your level as a percentage selects the desired creature type; otherwise roll the appropriate result normally.

changes: Druid casting level increases 16 → 17; daily slots remain six at each spell level 1–7. Extra longevity increases 160 → 170 years.

Gain entry to the Elemental Plane of Earth at will; transfer takes 1 round. Planar entry also makes the environment natural to you, with no time limit for remaining.
Gain conjure water elemental once per day; use the UA conjuring procedure and result table.

progression.label: Advanced XP reset track
progression.description: Continues the druid class through Grand Druid and Hierophant. After reaching at least 3,500,001 XP, a Grand Druid who finds a successor may abdicate and enter the level-16 Hierophant category with XP reset to 1. The reset begins a separate advancement scale within this druid progression.

sections.description: PHB pp. 32–33 presents combinations operated at the same time by non-human or semi-human characters. The combinations available depend on race; this is a separate procedure from changing professions.

sections.label: Sequential class change (dual-class)
sections.description: PHB p. 33’s human-only profession change stops advancement in the former class. It requires principal attribute scores of at least 15 in the original class and 17 or 18 in the new class, with alignment restrictions. The character retains earlier hit points but begins the new class’s other functions at level 1. Former-class functions restrict new-class XP until the new level exceeds the old one.

terminologyNotes: “Dual-class” is a navigation gloss here. PHB p. 33 heads its sequential rule “The Character With Two Classes.”

The bard appendix permits humans and half-elves, while the general two-class rule requires a human. The bard guide is classified by its appendix sequence rather than automatically assigned that general procedure.
For the bard’s thief-stage transition, PHB p. 117 says “between 5th and 9th.” This metadata retains that wording without resolving its boundary convention.
UA p. 23 calls thief-acrobat a “split-class” specialist; UA p. 25 otherwise treats the specialist as a thief except for the stated changes.
A Class track badge identifies one guide’s advancement table; it makes no finding about eligibility for a permitted race-based class combination.
